key_insight: Synthetic crystal structures can support diffusion pretraining for materials property prediction while reducing reliance on costly DFT-relaxed training structures.
engineering_relevance: Fast machine-learned relaxation and synthetic structure generation offer a scalable route to broader crystal training data without requiring quantum-mechanical property labels for every structure.
method: Generate crystals through perturb-and-relax, MatterGen sampling, and protostructure enumeration.
Use machine-learned interatomic potentials where structural relaxation is required.
Pretrain a randomly initialized Orb-v2 backbone with coordinate denoising, VP diffusion, or sub-VP diffusion.
evidence_signal: Every synthetic-pretraining condition numerically outperformed random initialization on seven MatBench tasks; scaling protostructures from 20k to 165k matched or exceeded MP-20k pretraining on most tasks in a study including an eighth task.
watch_item: The fixed 400-epoch scaling study increases both data diversity and optimization updates, so improvements cannot be attributed to dataset size alone.
paper_title: Synthetic Crystal Data Generation for Diffusion Pretraining in Material Property Prediction
